subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw native `tool_response` as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the repair chooses a public plugin hook payload and timing boundary across native-relay immediacy, app-server structured fidelity, and duplicate-event avoidance.

options.title: Use structured app-server projection
options.body: Make app-server command/file completion data the canonical plugin-visible result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw duplicate native event.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex shape
options.body: Keep OpenClaw relay behavior stable and ask Codex to include structured shell status in native PostToolUse, leaving this issue blocked until that contract exists.

options.title: Document raw string as intentional
options.body: Treat native `tool_response` strings as the supported contract and direct plugins to another surface for exit-code observability.

recommendation.title: Use structured app-server projection
recommendation.body: Make app-server command/file completion data the canonical plugin-visible result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw duplicate native event.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the public plugin hook/tool-result API boundary introduced by the harness middleware work.
